brief: c268, and the source's own sentence is the claim under test. BON_K's comment states: 'hash share of shed days offered one — 5-6 of the 7 in every year of 12 (histogram); the weather then takes ~2/3'. #178 then measured HEAD at 37 bonfires and its candidate at 44 over IDENTICAL hash-only calendars, because the fire COUNT rides on bonfireWeather() at TWO gates — the spawn hour and the match — and nobody has bounded that swing. Re-run the histogram over at least 6 seeds x 4 years, check the comment's numbers against what HEAD actually does, bound the weather's swing at both gates, and make the sentence TRUE. Rewriting the sentence to what is true is an equally good outcome and is the point of the `fidelity` kind: the artifact keeping a promise it already makes in its own comments. probes/bonfire-year.mjs and probes/bonfire-wind.mjs already exist — read them before writing a third.
successLooksLike: One number for offered shed days per year and one for fires actually lit, both with their spread across seeds, and the BON_K comment agreeing with them to the digit. The swing between two builds on identical calendars is bounded and stated.
avoid: Do not add a new weather term — #178 already showed both faces of ONE scalar are enough, and this is a fidelity job, not a deepening. Do not touch the burn model (bon.spent as a fuel budget) unless the histogram says the burn is where the count moves.
